name: lavat
desc: Lava lamp simulation using metaballs in the terminal
why: A metaball lava lamp simulation running in the terminal, something you can watch and nudge.

brief.what_it_is: lavat is a terminal program written in C that draws a lava lamp: a set of metaballs (blobs) that merge and separate on screen. You launch it from a shell with optional flags for color, speed, ball radius, ball count, rim, custom characters, gradient colors and gravity. Its output is a live animation in the terminal, and you can change speed, size, count and colors while it runs using single keys.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a 'little program that simulates a lava lamp in the terminal', a toy for watching the blobs drift in a terminal window. The gradient and gravity features were added later, and the credits point to a JavaScript lava lamp tutorial as the inspiration.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals beyond naming Termbox2 as the terminal library and mentioning that the -G mode simulates heating at the bottom, rising, cooling at the top and falling. Metaball rendering and ASCII character mapping are implied by the options (-F, -R, -r) but not described in detail.

brief.install_notes: Requirements per the README: a Unix-like system, a C compiler and make. Install by cloning the repo and running sudo make install. The README says the program is also packaged in other repositories (tracked via Repology), but it does not name a Homebrew formula specifically. No accounts, runtime or config files are mentioned. Tip: zoom the terminal out for better resolution.
brief.standout: Runtime keyboard controls let you reshape the lava while it runs (radius, rim, ball count, speed, colors, party mode), and the -F option lets you swap the ball glyphs for custom ASCII, with multi-character sets producing a faux-3D shading.
brief.status: Unknown for a release date: the README mentions no version and I found no release page. The commit history I could read shows commits from Jan 27, 2026 (gravity and buoyancy mode) and Aug 25, 2025 (README edits), with earlier commits back to 2022, so it has been touched recently. Maintained-looking, but I can't confirm beyond that.
brief.caveats: Unix-like systems only per the README. Wide or unicode characters may render broken with -F. The -C option may not work well with many balls or large radius. The -R rim option does not show with the default color, and Kitty/Alacritty users must pair it with -k. Building requires a C compiler and make; the sudo make install step writes system-wide. Repology packaging page could not be fetched, so packaging status is unverified.

entry.title: lavat
entry.tldr: A terminal lava lamp: metaball blobs drift, merge and split on screen, and you reshape them with single keystrokes while it runs.
entry.deeper_look:
lavat is a small C program that draws a lava lamp in the terminal. A set of blobs moves around, and when they get close they fuse into one shape and then pull apart again. Flags set the colour, speed, ball count, ball radius, rim, and the characters used to draw them. Most of these can also be changed with single keys while it is running.

The README calls it a "little program that simulates a lava lamp in the terminal", and that is the whole pitch. It is a toy to leave running in a spare pane. The credits point to a JavaScript lava lamp tutorial as the inspiration, and the terminal drawing is done with Termbox2.

The idea underneath is metaballs. Each blob is not a hard circle but a field that fades with distance. Where fields overlap they add up, and anything above a threshold is drawn. That is why two blobs bulge toward each other and join instead of just overlapping. The README does not describe the internals, but the options imply this approach. The `-F` flag swaps the glyphs for your own character set, and multi-character sets give a faux-3D shading.

The `-G` mode adds a bit of physics: per the README, balls heat up at the bottom, rise, cool at the top, then fall. The gradient and gravity features were added after the original, with gravity landing in January 2026.
entry.install:
brew install lavat
# Needs a Unix-like system. Zoom your terminal out before running for finer resolution. The README's own route is: git clone https://github.com/AngelJumbo/lavat, then sudo make install (needs a C compiler and make).

try_this.what_happens: Runs the default lamp with named colours, green blobs and a red rim colour.
Gradient colours with gravity and buoyancy: 8 balls of radius 10 with a rim of 3, rising and falling.
Draws the blobs with custom characters, giving a shaded, almost 3D look.

entry.whats_unique: You can reshape the lamp live from the keyboard, and the custom glyph option turns the blobs into shaded ASCII art. The gravity mode makes them behave like heated wax rather than drifting at random.
entry.caveats: Unix-like systems only; wide or unicode characters can render badly with -F, and the -R rim will not show with the default colour unless you also set -k.
